Subject: [PillarTech] intermittent poor-quality outputs — sample included

Hi Jonas,

We hit a couple of cases this morning where model responses looked garbled — missing sentences and odd tokenization. It’s impacting a small percentage of our customers but it’s visible in our task logs. I attached a screenshot and a truncated request/response pair.

Can the Redwood team confirm whether there’s a recent model change or infra incident that could explain this? If we can get a quick triage it would be appreciated — our CS team is already fielding questions.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Integrations
PillarTech

Attachments: pillartech_screenshot_120326.png (image/png), request-response-sample.txt (text/plain)

Hi Elena — thanks for the report and for sending the sample. We’re not seeing any platform-wide incidents in the last 24 hours, but I’ve looped in Lauren (SRE) and Marissa (CS lead) to do a focused triage on your specific request IDs.

Quick asks while we investigate: can you confirm the model and model_version you observed in the sample, and whether you were using Redwood’s hosted API or your Dedicated pool? Any additional request headers (max_tokens, temperature) would help speed repro.

We’ll get back with an initial update within two business hours.

—Jonas

Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [PillarTech] intermittent poor-quality outputs — sample included

Team — triage notes below (internal).

Steps taken:
- Pulled request_id from Elena’s sample and replayed against the same model (redwood/gptx-3.1) in our staging fleet and in their Dedicated pool (we have access to their Dedicated staging account for reproductions).
- Replays completed at both 1x and with original client headers (temperature=0.7, max_tokens=256).
- Collected server-side logs and tokenization traces; attached consolidated logs (redwood_logs_120326.txt).

Findings:
- The responses from staging and Dedicated replay matched expected output and did not show truncation or garbling.
- No kernel crashes, padding issues, or memory anomalies in the time window of the original request. CPU/GPU telemetry normal.
- The tokenization trace shows the prompt was tokenized as expected; no partial token corruption.

Hypothesis and next steps:
- Candidate cause is client-side: a post-processing step or UI truncation when rendering results. Elena’s screenshot shows a truncated UI viewport that could be confused for a model defect.
- Ask PillarTech to provide the raw API response body for the failing events (not a screenshot), and confirm whether they do any downstream trimming or concatenation in their rendering layer.

I’ll continue watching logs and will re-run replays if PillarTech provides additional raw payloads.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments (internal): redwood_logs_120326.txt

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@pillartech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Investigation concluded — no platform issue identified

Hi Elena — final update from our side.

Summary:
- We replayed the exact request against the same model and observed identical, correct responses in both Redwood hosted and your Dedicated pool (see attached logs).
- Infrastructure telemetry (kernels, memory, runtime) shows no error or anomaly during the reported window.
- The raw API payload you pasted matches our replays, indicating the model output itself was intact.

Conclusion:
- At this time we have not found evidence of a Redwood model or serving infrastructure bug. The most likely root cause is downstream client-side rendering in PillarTech’s in-app preview (timing/concatenation or a browser/UI truncation edge-case).

Recommended next steps for PillarTech (we’re happy to help):
1) Capture a reproducible failing example including network logs, raw API response bodies, and a brief video of the UI failing to render correctly.
2) Try serving the raw API payload directly into a minimal rendering page to confirm whether the issue reproduces without your UI stack.
3) If you want Redwood to pair on a live debug session, Marissa can coordinate a time (I’ve cc’d her).

If you capture a raw response that looks corrupted (different from what we saw), please re-open the ticket and we’ll prioritize a deeper infra investigation. Otherwise, I’m going to close this incident on our side.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
